title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lawrence, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lawrence, PA
metaDescription: Lawrence, PA sits in Washington County's core Marcellus wet-gas territory. See how the sale process works from first call to closing.
heroLead: Lawrence is a small Washington County community sitting inside some of the most actively drilled wet-gas Marcellus acreage in the state.
intro: Washington County doesn't need much of an introduction if you've owned land here for a while — it's been at the center of Marcellus development since the play's earliest days, and Lawrence sits right inside that activity. Most families we talk to here already have some history with gas leasing, whether it's an active lease from years ago or a unit that's been filed but not yet drilled.

sections.heading: Step One: Confirming What You Actually Own
paragraphs: We start every Lawrence-area file by pulling the deed and any recorded lease or assignment against it. Washington County's records are extensive given how much leasing activity has happened here over the years, so it's common to find several layers of history to work through before we can say clearly what's currently unencumbered.

Because Washington County has seen so much leasing turnover over the years, it's not unusual for a Lawrence-area parcel to have two or three recorded documents layered on top of each other, and untangling that order is part of the work we do before any offer goes out.

sections.heading: Step Two: Checking Unit and Production Status
paragraphs: If a unit has been filed that includes your Lawrence property, we look at whether it's producing, permitted, or still pending, and if there's royalty history already, we review that too. This tells us whether we're valuing an interest with a real track record or one that's still speculative.

sections.heading: Step Three: An Honest Range, Then Your Decision
paragraphs: Once we've gone through the deed and unit history, we put together a written range tied to what we actually found, not a flat number pulled from a general market average. You take the time you need to review it, ask questions, or bring in an attorney before deciding.

faqs.question: I already have a lease on my Lawrence property — can I still sell?
faqs.answer: Yes, an existing lease doesn't prevent a sale of the underlying mineral rights, though it does affect how the interest is valued and structured.

faqs.question: How much has Washington County actually been drilled?
faqs.answer: Extensively — it's consistently one of the top Marcellus wet-gas counties in Pennsylvania by well count and production.

faqs.question: What's the first document I should look for?
faqs.answer: Your deed, and if you have it, any lease paperwork. If you can't find either, we can pull them from the Washington County recorder's office.

faqs.question: What if the recorded lease on my Lawrence property looks outdated?
faqs.answer: Older leases sometimes have terms that no longer reflect current market practice; we review whether it's still valid and how it affects a sale before quoting anything.
